key_insight: PoliVEM unifies multiple solid-mechanics formulations in a single Python-driven VEM framework by sharing mesh, DOF, projection, assembly, and solver infrastructure across element types.
engineering_relevance: It provides a reusable computational core for beams, elasticity, diffusion, and hyperelasticity, making it attractive for rapid development and testing of polygonal/polyhedral solid mechanics solvers.
method: C++17 core with Python interface for 1D beams, 2D/3D elasticity, axisymmetric elasticity, diffusion, and finite-strain hyperelasticity.
Common hierarchy for vertex, edge, face, and cell degrees of freedom with cached polynomial projections and element-level consistency–stabilization split.
Modular composition of mesh, material, element, assembler, and solver, plus static condensation, coloured sparse assembly, and Newton/time-integration solvers.
evidence_signal: The framework is evaluated with numerical experiments on polynomial reproduction, static condensation recovery, higher-order DOFs, polygonal/polyhedral meshes, patch tests, stiffness spectra, and comparisons against independent finite element results.
watch_item: High-order polynomial bases on anisotropic cells and the memory cost of sparse direct factorization are identified as current limitations.
paper_title: PoliVEM: a Python-driven virtual element framework for computational solid mechanics
